name: Julia Cao
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember offering a meal subsidy at a shop too small for forms.” Monday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Julia stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I want the port to subsidize a workers' meal without owning the menu or the cook's schedule.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Julia has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Julia steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: Julia finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To secure a port subsidy without surrendering the menu.
family: Dale Malik is Julia’s stepsibling. Julia is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Dale calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Salt in the pockets*, Dale says, “I kept the salt from my last deck shift in my cuff.”
connections: Orlando Dinh. A port employee's need for breakfast and a union subsidy get considered alongside the cook's time.

reactions.response: Julia checks what the earlier start would do to the cook's family breakfast.
